blocking: Protocol/code mismatch, diagnostics: protocol.json diagnostics_reported asks for Spearman 'between WT_r13, WT_r14, ST_r6, ST_r7' (6 pairs) plus LBRKO_r13~LBRKO_r14; lbr.py:99-100 computes only 5 pairs (missing WT_r13~ST_r7 and WT_r14~ST_r6). Add the missing pairs (and WT_r13~LBRKO_r13, WT_r14~LBRKO_r14, which the FL-attenuation check below needs) or narrow the protocol text before freeze.

Overstated independence of B: protocol.json sample_notes says ST noise is 'independent of every primary delta', then hedges. GEO shows ST_r6 = GSM8523514 (title SunTag_SCII_LB2_Cal_r6) is deposited as ..._CAL_r13_... and ST_r7 = GSM8523520 as ..._CAL_r14_...; the rNN in these file names is the lab's experiment number shared with iCUT r13/r14, so treat each ST sample as processed in the same pA-DamID experiment as the iCUT r13/r14 samples, not 'may share'. Restate: B is a different subline (RPE1_SunTag_170_10, DMEM vs DMEM:F12) with a batch component shared with both primaries (the mean over r13 and r14 keeps it symmetric), and add this to disclosed_limits. Also PL_line (ST_r6 - ST_r7) is really a second cross-batch (r13 vs r14) placebo in another line, not a 'line' placebo; rename or re-describe it.

Add the flattening-control attenuation limit to disclosed_limits and report its size: quantile-mapping a noisy WT onto a noisy KO marginal (lbr.py:29-34, 79-80) gives an effective slope sd(KO)/sd(WT) that is larger than the true flattening slope a whenever KO has a larger noise-to-signal ratio (a flatter profile with the same absolute noise), so FL understates the leak. Reviewer simulation with test_lbr.world, gc_effect=0 and st_noise=1.2: FL/primary rho ratio = 1.05 at noise 0.15, 0.95 at 0.4, 0.67-0.71 at 0.7. The 0.5*m bound still catches pure flattening in all of these, but the margin shrinks as noise grows. Report the KO and WT replicate Spearman correlations and a reported-only disattenuated FL (sim = a_hat*WT_other, where a_hat = cov(KO_rX, WT_other)/(var(WT_other)*reliability_WT), with reliability taken from WT_r13~WT_r14) so a reader can check the margin.
minor: lbr/freeze.json does not exist yet; fetch() (lbr.py:17-18) and run() (lbr.py:87-88) both need it. Freeze protocol.json, lbr.py, test_lbr.py, code/screen.py, panel/panel.py and features/tiles.tsv before any fetch.
run() never re-checks data files against lbr/intake.json (lbr.py:85-95). Add an intake sha256 assert for every sample file.

No synthetic world has a cross-batch GC bias, so removing the placebo guard (lbr.py:63) is caught only by the hand-built test_label_rules. Add a world where WT_r13/LBRKO_r13 carry +c*zgc and r14 carry -c*zgc, and assert DIRECTION_ONLY.

FL_r13 and FL_r14 carry the cross-batch term with opposite signs (FL_r13 contains +r14 - r13 batch bias, FL_r14 the reverse), so a batch GC bias pushes one FL up and the other down. Requiring both FL < 0.5*m makes this conservative, and PL_batch bounds it; say so in the rationale.

The 0.5*m bounds compare point estimates with no allowance for sampling error in FL or PL. Prior null SD was about 0.02 (damid/results/result.json), which is fine for m >= 0.1 but tight near m = 0.05. Disclose this, or report FL - P with its shift-null SD.

flex_basis (lbr.py:36-41) ranks b over all finite tiles, not over the ok subset used in test_design (lbr.py:45-48). This is harmless (only a rescale), but it differs from the protocol wording 'rank(B)/n'.

The abort rule (lbr.py:108) also aborts the whole run when a secondary (T2B) test fails n/finite. This is consistent with 'any test' but lets a reported-only readout veto the primary label; state that it is intended.

Better or alternative baselines: the only other deposited RPE1_iCUT WT control tracks are GSM9146390/GSM9146396 (WT_CT20 r17/r18). They are the same line as the primaries and come from separate experiments, but their metadata conflicts (title Lmnb2, description 'control_DMSO, RPE1, Lmnb1', antibody field empty) and they are DMSO-treated. Keeping ST as the primary B is defensible. These could be a reported-only sensitivity baseline, but only if the antibody is confirmed. Do not use the ST *_calibrated.bw variants; the chosen 20kb log2 files match the iCUT processing.
notes: Sample mapping verified against GEO: WT_r13=GSM8523526 iCUT_WT_SCII_LB2_r1; WT_r14=GSM8523538 _r2; LBRKO_r13=GSM8523532 iCUT_LBRKO_SCII_LB2_r1 (LBRKO+control_siRNA); LBRKO_r14=GSM8523544 _r2; ST_r6=GSM8523514 SunTag_SCII_LB2_Cal_r6; ST_r7=GSM8523520 _Cal_r7; WT_T2B_r13/r14=GSM8523529/GSM8523541; LBRKO_T2B_r13/r14=GSM8523535/GSM8523547. All are LaminB2 20 kb log2(target/Dam) hg38 files, and the GSM8523nnn URL directory is right for all of them. The label logic (lbr.py:58-73) matches protocol labels and final_rule exactly. The seed order (tests_for dict order, lbr.py:77-82) matches the statistic text, and the flexible arm uses +100. The linear arm matches test_pair with [tss, B] ranked, and the flexible design matches the protocol basis. min_n 3000 against 5760 autosomal tiles is fine. The FL design is sound in structure: it uses the same iCUT WT, the same B and the same residualization as the primaries, so line differences between iCUT and ST and the measurement error in B leak equally into FL and P, and the flexible arm cannot remove that leak, which is why FL is the operative guard. Limits a SUPPORTED label must carry beyond those already listed: n=1 KO clone vs n=1 WT line (the two 'batches' are technical/experimental repeats of one contrast, so SUPPORTED is about this clone pair); LMNB2 in RPE1 vs LMNB1 in K562 at origin; the sign contrast with LMNA is cross-cohort only; the published paper's LBR-KO findings were available to the authors even though the data were not opened; and FL attenuation as above. Nothing else would make SUPPORTED misleading if the claim_ceiling wording is kept.
